items.title: Chevening Europe Defence and Security Fellowship | Chevening
items.text:
Hosted by Cranfield University

Overview

The Chevening Europe Defence and Security Fellowship is funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) and delivered by Cranfield University at the Defence Academy of the United Kingdom, Shrivenham. This Fellowship is open to all non-ODA eligible European countries.
The fellowship is designed for mid-career professionals from across Europe who have demonstrated leadership potential in security and defence. The programme aims to develop leaders capable of operating effectively within complex and rapidly changing security and defence contexts. It provides an interdisciplinary and applied learning experience that strengthens participants’ understanding of the strategic challenges facing governments, international organisations, and public institutions.
Through six weeks of teaching, discussion, practical exercises, site visits, individual research, and collaborative learning, fellows will develop practical insight into leadership, organisational resilience, governance, strategic decision-making, cyber resilience, artificial intelligence, and international collaboration. The programme also creates lasting professional networks across Europe and the UK.

Duration

The duration of this fellowship is six weeks and there will be two cohorts:

- Cohort 1: 25 January – 5 March 2027
- Cohort 2: 15 March – 23 April 2027

More about the programme

Ready to take your leadership in security and cyber policy to the next level?

Fellows will be encouraged to:

- Critically evaluate contemporary strategic, organisational, and leadership challenges.
- Analyse how organisational culture, human behaviour, and governance influence institutional effectiveness, resilience, and vulnerability.
- Assess the opportunities and risks associated with cyber security, artificial intelligence, and emerging technologies.
- Apply strategic decision-making approaches in situations characterised by uncertainty, competing pressures, and incomplete information.
- Collaborate effectively across cultural, professional, and national boundaries to develop informed responses to complex organisational and societal challenges.

The programme is organised around six integrated themes:

- Global Leadership in an Era of Complexity
- Understanding People, Culture, and Organisations
- Cyber Resilience and Information Threats
- Artificial Intelligence, Governance, and Emerging Technology
- Strategic Decision-Making Under Pressure
- Building Resilience and Future Leadership

Fellows will benefit from lectures, workshops, simulations, practitioner speakers, research activity, UK institutional visits, and opportunities to build enduring international professional networks.

Throughout the programme, fellows will work on a research project addressing a relevant policy, leadership, organisational, or security challenge. They will receive academic support as they develop their work and will present their findings to the FCDO in London at the end of the fellowship.

Keep an eye on our channels to be the first to know when applications open again

Stay up to date

Eligibility

In addition to meeting our standard eligibility criteria, you must:

- Be a citizen of and resident in one of the following countries at the point of application: Andorra, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Gibraltar, Greece, Holy See, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Monaco, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, San Marino, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, or Switzerland.

-

If you live in a European overseas territory, you may apply through the relevant Chevening award scheme for the European country of which you are a citizen.

- Hold a postgraduate qualification (or equivalent professional training or experience in a relevant field).
- Have at least five years’ relevant professional experience.
- Be a mid-career professional with responsibilities for national or international security, and employed within government, public or private sector, academia, defence, security, law enforcement, intelligence, civil protection, resilience, or an international organisation.
- Be working in a role with the potential to influence organisational capability, policy, strategy, or operational effectiveness within their organisation and/or country.
- Be able to demonstrate leadership potential and a commitment to applying the knowledge and networks gained through the fellowship within their organisation and/or country on completion of the programme.

Funding and benefits

Each fellowship includes:

- Full programme fees

- Living expenses for the duration of the fellowship, including pre-arranged accommodation close to Oxford

- Return economy airfare

Relevant sectors and professional experience

- Military personnel and civilian defence staff
- Government officials, diplomats and international relationship managers
- HR, people and organisational development professionals
- Leaders and managers in defence and security institutions, and related industries
- Police, intelligence and emergency planning professionals
- Cybersecurity, technology and information specialists
- Energy, infrastructure and supply chain professionals
- Journalists, researchers and academics working on relevant issues
- Professionals in international organisations and civil society
- Local authority staff and their equivalents in other countries
- Policy makers and policy advisers

The programme’s focus on leadership, people and organisations, technology, decision-making and resilience means applicants may bring different forms of experience. These examples are illustrative, not exhaustive. The Fellowship welcomes applicants from any field with a connection to defence or security and the ambition to put what they learn into practice.

The future of cybersecurity won’t be defined by technology alone, but by the people who know how to navigate it.

Applications for the Chevening Western Balkans Cyber Security Fellowship are open until 6 March 2024. University professor Angelina Stanojoska shares her experience on the programme.

Chevening Fellow Vivek Yadav exemplifies leadership at the intersection of technology and national security

items.title: Chevening LSE Global Impact Fellowship | Chevening
items.text:
Hosted by the London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE)

Overview

The Chevening LSE Global Impact Fellowship is funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office.

It’s for mid-career professionals from China who are interested in carrying out research in key thematic areas.

The programme welcomes applications across all social science disciplines, with a particular emphasis on international relations; public policy and administration; public diplomacy; social, economic, and environmental policy; and development studies.

The fellowship will take place at the London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE).

Duration

The duration of this fellowship is three or six.

- Start: October
- End: December or March (depends on the duration)

More about the programme

Are you ready to invest in your professional development and collaborate with world-class academics?

The Chevening LSE Global Impact Fellowship allows three successful applicants to work on a defined research project at LSE.

Applicants are not required to secure an advisor at LSE when applying, but it is helpful if they have someone in mind they would like to work with or engage with during the fellowship.

Once selected, fellows are expected to identify and secure an advisor, and will be hosted in a department, institute, or centre at LSE in line with their research interests.

During their time at LSE, fellows are expected to work on their research and complete a paper, which they will then present at the end of the fellowship. Fellows may also audit relevant lectures (subject to instructor approval) and participate in seminars and discussion groups.

Please note, all applications must include a research proposal.

Keep an eye on our channels to be the first to know when applications open again

Stay up to date

Eligibility

In addition to meeting our standard eligibility criteria, you must:

- Be a citizen of China, currently live in the country, and intend to return to China at the end of the period of study

- Hold a postgraduate (PG) level qualification (or equivalent professional training or experience in a relevant area) at the time of application

- Have at least five years’ work experience prior to applying or be currently enrolled as a PhD candidate (PhD must not be with a UK/EU or USA university)

Additionally, strong applicants are expected to have:

- An excellent academic track record and a demonstrated interest in the chosen area of research, measured by previous professional development and work-related experience and projects and/or research output, including, but not limited to, journal articles, policy papers, reports, and other forms of publications

- Enthusiasm for engaging with LSE’s intellectual community and contributing to their host department’s academic activities

Funding and benefits

Each fellowship includes:

- Full programme fees

- Living expenses for the duration of the fellowship

- Return economy airfare

- Allowance package for research-related activities

Hear from our fellows

You should apply for this fellowship because it gives you a chance to refresh, recharge, and reset yourself.

Yuan Ming
Chevening LSE Fellow

items.title: Chevening Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies (OCIS) | Chevening
items.text:
Chevening Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies Fellowship (OCIS) Fellowship

Hosted by the Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies

Overview

The Chevening Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies (OCIS) Fellowship is a collaboration between the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office and the OCIS.

It is open to applications from mid-career professionals and academics who are dedicated to promoting academic activities that encourage a more informed understanding of the culture and civilisation of Islam and contemporary Muslim societies.

Fellows will learn how to engage with complex global challenges through the lens of Islamic thought, diplomacy, and contemporary policy, while deepening their understanding of international relations, interfaith dialogue, and leadership in diverse cultural contexts.

The fellowship will take place at the Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies.

Duration

The duration of this fellowship is five months.

- Start: October
- End: March

More about the programme

Are you ready to explore the intersection of faith, leadership, and global policy, and contribute to meaningful dialogue and understanding between the Islamic world and the wider international community?

The Chevening Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies (OCIS) Fellowships offer a unique opportunity for six exceptional candidates to undertake self-directed research focusing on their own project.

Fellows will have the opportunity to:

- Explore the culture, civilisation, and historical trajectories of Muslim societies

- Foster inter‑civilisational dialogue and academic exchange

- Discuss issues relating to the Islamic world, including Islamic history, classical Islamic sciences, economics and Islamic finance, public health, science and technology in the Muslim world, and the study of Muslims in the West

Fellows will gain:

- Access to world-class academic resources and mentorship

- Opportunities for intercultural dialogue and intellectual exchange

- Enhanced leadership skills and policy insight

When submitting your application, you should be prepared to outline a short proposal on the area of academic research you would like to conduct. The proposal should include a main research question and how you intend to conduct this research while in residence at the centre.

The Chevening Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies Fellowship (OCIS) Fellowship selection process involves two rounds of interviews. The first interview will be with British embassies and high commissions. You should be prepared to explain your suitability and motivations for the Chevening OCIS Fellowship, and you should also be prepared to explain your research interests. Successful candidates will be invited to a second and final interview with representatives from OCIS, which will focus further on your research interests.

Please note that the FCDO is unable to assist with arranging or facilitating travel to the UK, including from Palestine. Successful fellows will need to arrange their own travel to the UK, potentially through third countries.

Keep an eye on our channels to be the first to know when applications open again

Stay up to date

Eligibility

In addition to meeting our standard eligibility criteria, you must:

- Be a citizen of one of the following countries and resident in one of these countries at the point of application: Afghanistan*, Algeria, Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Egypt, Indonesia, Iraq, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Lebanon, Libya, Malaysia, Morocco, Nigeria, Pakistan, Palestine, Philippines, Senegal, Sudan*, Syria, Tajikistan, Tunisia, Türkiye, Turkmenistan, or Uzbekistan

- Hold a postgraduate level qualification (or equivalent professional training or experience in a relevant area) at the time of application

- Have significant professional and/or academic research experience (at least five years)

*Please note: Under recent UK Government legislation, Afghanistan and Sudan citizens are unable to obtain a Study Visa to enter the UK; however, this does not affect fellowship visa routes. Afghanistan and Sudan citizens are still eligible to apply for the Chevening OCIS Fellowship. For the most up-to-date information, please visit the UK Government website. We are unable to provide any further guidance beyond what is published there.

Funding and benefits

Each fellowship includes:

- Five-month period of research at OCIS

- Living expenses for the duration of the fellowship

- Return economy airfare

- Allowance package for research-related activities

Hear from our fellows

For my work on my book, I couldn’t have thought of a more perfect place than OCIS. I found myself in the company of colleagues who have published many books and I got to learn handy tips from them about my own project. Pursuing research at the University of Oxford, I was afforded many opportunities to attend talks on a large number of topics organised by the different colleges across the city.

Dr Abdur Rehman Cheema
Chevening OCIS Fellow

items.title: Chevening British Library Southeast Asian Fellowship | Chevening
items.text:
Hosted by the British Library

Apply today

Overview

The Chevening British Library Southeast Asian Fellowship is co-funded by the British Library and the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office.

It is open to applications from mid-career professionals from Cambodia, Laos, and Thailand, who have a strong interest in surveying, assessing, and researching rare, printed works.

If selected, you will undertake a research project on the British Library’s collection of early printed works in Cambodian, Lao, and Thai languages, covering the period from c.1840 to 1950 (c.600-800 items). You will provide metadata-style information in original scripts and Romanisation as the basis for the creation of catalogue records by the supervising curator.

The fellowship will take place at the British Library, where you will work closely with the Henry Ginsburg Curator, Ms Jana Igunma, who is responsible for this collection of early printed materials, as well as other colleagues in the Southeast Asia section and the British Library’ Conservation Centre.

The British Library’s Asian and African Collections hold the UK’s largest and most significant collection of Thai, Lao, and Khmer language printed materials, comprising more than 10,000 books and ephemera and over 50 periodicals. The collection includes exceptional examples of early printing from Thailand, Laos, and Cambodia, many of which are unique or extremely rare.

Duration

The duration of this fellowship is 12 months.

- Start: September 2027
- End: September 2028

More about the programme

Despite the international significance of these collections, much of the material remains under-researched, particularly in relation to its content, design, printing technologies, and historical importance. Many items remain accessible only through historic card catalogues, while approximately 200 early Thai publications have yet to be catalogued.
This fellowship offers a unique opportunity to survey, assess, and research rare, printed works in Thai, Lao, and Khmer languages. The project will improve discoverability by creating metadata that supports comprehensive catalogue records, identifying conservation priorities, and informing future digitisation initiatives.

Working with a collection that documents the transition from manuscript to print culture across Southeast Asia, you will contribute directly to making these remarkable resources more accessible to researchers, students, heritage organisations, and communities around the world.

Fellows will have the opportunity to:

- Review, identify, and research early printed works in Cambodian, Lao, and Thai languages and scripts
- Create metadata in original scripts and Romanisation to support catalogue creation
- Work with curators, conservation specialists, and digital specialists at the British Library
- Contribute to the understanding of Southeast Asian printing history, book culture, and manuscript traditions
- Write and publish a blog post and/or journal article highlighting project findings
- Organise a show-and-tell session or staff presentation showcasing the collections
- Participate in public engagement activities with heritage communities and wider audiences
- Present findings at a national or international symposium or conference

Fellows will gain:

- Specialist expertise in metadata creation for Southeast Asian early printed collections
- Experience working with rare books and heritage collections in a world-leading research library
- Insights into curatorial practice, conservation, digitisation, and collection management
- Experience using digital tools and AI-assisted approaches to support metadata creation
- Opportunities to build national and international professional networks
- Enhanced experience communicating research to both specialist and non-specialist audiences

Ready to turn your ambitions and experiences into lasting change?

Apply Today

Eligibility criteria:

In addition to meeting our standard eligibility criteria, you must:

- Be a citizen of and resident in one of the following countries: Cambodia, Laos, and Thailand
- Have a postgraduate level qualification (or equivalent professional training or experience in a relevant area) at the time of application
- Have significant professional and/or academic research experience (at least five years)
- Be currently employed or enrolled as a PhD candidate (your PhD must not be with a UK/EU or USA university)
- Have excellent written and spoken knowledge of Thai, Lao, and Khmer, or excellent knowledge of Thai together with either Lao or Khmer
- Have good written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate research findings effectively
- Have an interest in bibliographical description, cataloguing, and curatorial work
- Have a willingness to learn and apply digital tools, including AI-assisted approaches, to support the creation of metadata
- Have experience of communicating with non-specialist audiences, including through blogs, social media, or other public engagement activities
- Have an interest in the history of Southeast Asian printing, book culture, and manuscript traditions

Funding and benefits

Each fellowship includes:

- 12-month period of project-based activity at the British Library
- Living expenses for the duration of the fellowship
- Return economy airfare
- Allowance package for fellowship-related activities
- Up to £1,000 for approved project-related expenses

items.title: Chevening British Library Coptic Collections Fellowship | Chevening
items.text:
Hosted by the British Library

Apply today

Overview

The Chevening British Library Coptic Collections Fellowship is co-funded by the British Library and the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office.

It is open to applications from mid-career professionals from Egypt, Palestine, and Sudan, who have a strong interest in Coptic manuscript heritage and cultural collections.

The British Library holds one of the world’s most significant collections of Coptic manuscripts, comprising hundreds of complete and fragmentary codices, as well as papyrus, parchment, and paper fragments documenting more than 1,500 years of Coptic history, theology, and literary culture. This internationally important collection provides unique insights into the history of Christianity, Egypt’s cultural heritage, manuscript production, and scholarly traditions.

The fellowship will take place at the British Library, where you will work closely with Dr. Michael Erdman, Head of Asian and African Studies (interim) to lead a research project.

You will use your language skills, subject expertise, and professional experience to survey the British Library’s Coptic holdings, enhance catalogue records, investigate collection provenance, and develop new opportunities for public and community engagement.

Duration

The duration of this fellowship is 12 months.

- Start: September 2027
- End: September 2028

More about the programme

Many parts of the British Library’s Coptic collections remain difficult to discover because a comprehensive overview of the holdings has never been produced. This fellowship offers a unique opportunity to address this challenge by contributing to the documentation, interpretation, and promotion of these remarkable manuscripts.

Working with manuscript collections that span over 15 centuries, you will help improve access to valuable resources. You will also contribute to a growing programme of provenance research that seeks to better understand the history of the collections and their acquisition.

This fellowship also supports the British Library’s work with the London Diocese of the Coptic Orthodox Church, creating opportunities to engage directly with heritage communities while developing new ways of sharing knowledge about the collections.

Fellows will have the opportunity to:

- Survey the British Library’s Coptic collections and identify gaps in existing cataloguing and documentation.
- Create and enhance catalogue records using manuscript evidence and existing metadata.
- Research, document, and analyse the provenance of manuscripts to improve understanding of the history and acquisition of the collections.
- Organise and contribute to events with Coptic community members and researchers.
- Produce blogs, reports, and other outputs that raise awareness of the Library’s Coptic collections.
- Contribute to public engagement activities that promote wider access to, and understanding of, Coptic heritage.

Fellows will gain:

- Experience working with one of the world’s leading research libraries and cultural heritage institutions.
- Opportunities to increase their international academic and professional profile.
- Specialist experience in manuscript cataloguing, provenance research, and collections documentation.
- Practical experience of planning and delivering community and public engagement activities around heritage collections.
- The opportunity to contribute to the future accessibility and interpretation of a globally significant collection.

Ready to turn your ambitions and experiences into lasting change?

Apply Today

Eligibility criteria

In addition to meeting our standard eligibility criteria, you must:

- Be citizens of Egypt, Sudan, or Palestine. Applicants should normally be resident in one of these countries, however citizens of these countries who are resident elsewhere in the Middle East and North Africa region in Chevening eligible, ODA-eligible countries (Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Morocco, Syria, Tunisia, Yemen) may also apply. Applicants must demonstrate a clear intention to return to and contribute to their country of citizenship following the fellowship and must return there for at least one year after the fellowship ends
- Have a postgraduate level qualification (or equivalent professional training or experience in a relevant area) at the time of application
- Have significant professional and/or academic research experience (at least five years)
- Be currently employed or enrolled as a PhD candidate (your PhD must not be with a UK/EU or USA university)
- Have excellent knowledge of Coptic (Sahidic or Bohairic), with knowledge of Arabic and/or Greek desirable
- Have good written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate research findings effectively
- Have experience of cataloguing and handling manuscript collections, with knowledge of manuscript description standards
- Have experience of provenance research and documentation, or a demonstrable interest in this area
- Have experience of working with heritage communities or delivering engagement activities related to cultural heritage collections

Funding and benefits

Each fellowship includes:

- 12-month period of project-based activity at the British Library
- Living expenses for the duration of the fellowship
- Return economy airfare
- Allowance package for fellowship-related activities
- Up to £1,000 for approved project-related expenses

Please note that the FCDO is unable to assist with arranging or facilitating travel to the UK, including from Palestine. Successful fellows will need to arrange their own travel to the UK, potentially through third countries.
